subject: BrightCart embeddings + reranker integration — post-call actions
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Mays <elena@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightCart — post-demo summary & next steps

Hi Elena / BrightCart team,

Thanks again for the demo earlier today — really appreciated the clear signal on your priority: improve relevance for category and search ranking while keeping tail latency under 80ms for the user-facing rerank step. Quick recap + proposed owners and next actions from our side: 

1) Current state (what you told us):
   - Provider: Vectorly (managed FAISS HNSW); vector dim = 768; L2-normalized; currently doing offline reindexes nightly.
   - Batch sizes: you reported ingest batches up to ~256 vectors; real-time scoring batch 8–32.
   - Reranker: candidate set ~50, scoring model separate (ours would be a neural reranker on top of semantic fetch).

2) Primary asks:
   - Migration plan that avoids regressions in ranking and keeps pup-to-prod latency safe.
   - Auth: SSO (OIDC) + service tokens for backend-to-backend calls; support for VPC/private endpoint.
   - SDK quickstart and example for structured output + tool-calling (we discussed a hybrid fetch->rerank pipeline).
   - Observability: token-level cost estimates + per-route latency breakdown.

3) Suggested immediate next steps (owners):
   - Sergio (me): send this recap and attach the initial SOW + security snapshot. (Done — attachments included.)
   - Marissa: provide a migration checklist (index compatibility, dim alignment, reindex cadence, fallbacks to Vectorly) and recommended quantization/profile options for cost savings.
   - Karthik: propose SDK auth patterns (OIDC flows, key rotation, sample routing rules for canary traffic) and a small sandbox token for BrightCart engineers.

4) Milestone proposal:
   - Sandbox access + example repo: within 3 business days.
   - Migration POC (sanity reindex + reranker validation): 2 weeks.
   - Production cutoff plan and rollback window: defined in SOW.

Environment / constraints you flagged: VPC requirement for PCI/SOC reasons; long-term desire to move to 1024 dims if we see quality uplift (we should benchmark first).

Please reply with any corrections. Elena — can you confirm the current nightly reindex window (approx UTC hours) and whether you have offline evaluation sets you can share (anonymized) so we can run a quick DCG/Recall comparison?

Thanks —
Sergio

On Thu, Jun 28, 2028 at 3:12 PM Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo earlier today — really appreciated the clear signal on your priority: improve relevance for category and search ranking while keeping tail latency under 80ms for the user-facing rerank step.

Thanks Sergio — great writeup. A few clarifications/corrections from our side: 

- Reindex window: currently runs between 02:00–04:00 UTC nightly.
- Provider: yes, Vectorly using FAISS HNSW on an AWS-hosted cluster.
- Vector details: 768 dims, L2 normalization on write.
- Batching: ingest bursts can hit 512 for backfill; live scoring budgets ~16 vectors per request on average.
- Reranker: we use a small on-prem transformer for final scoring; we'd like Redwood to integrate into our fetch->rerank flow and optionally power the semantic fetch so we can drop some CPU from the on-prem cluster.
- Security: we need OIDC SSO for developer consoles and a private endpoint (VPC) for production.

We can share a small evaluation set (anonymized queries + ground truth clicks) — I will share with Marissa’s account on Drive once we've redacted customer-identifying fields.

Two asks from us now:
1) Can you confirm the supported ANN libraries/indices for the hosted dedicated offering (FAISS, HNSW, IVF, etc.) and whether Redwood can export an index snapshot compatible with FAISS for rollback?
2) On dim migration: we are open to exploring 1024 but will need an estimation of the reindex cost (time + compute) and whether you support incremental migrations (keep 768 index as fallback).

Happy to have a technical call next week — prefer Tue/Wed mornings PT.

Best,
Elena
Elena Mays
Head of Platform Engineering | BrightCart
elena@brightcart.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Mays <elena@brightcart.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightCart — post-demo summary & next steps

Hi Elena — thanks for the details and for offering the eval set. Below is a pragmatic checklist and answers to your two asks.

Quick answers up front:
- Supported ANN/index types (hosted & dedicated): FAISS (Flat, IVF, HNSW), HNSWlib-compatible, and we provide a managed HNSW variant for strict latency SLOs.
- Index export/rollback: we can export snapshots in FAISS-compatible format (snapshot + meta) so you can keep a rollback copy that Vectorly could ingest.
- Dimension migration: we support an incremental migration pattern — run a parallel 1024 index, shadow-serve small percentage of traffic (canary), measure reranker impact; fallback to 768 index automatically on quality/latency regression.

Migration checklist (POC -> Prod):
1) Sandbox setup (owner: Karthik): create VPC-peered sandbox and issue a sandbox service token for BrightCart engineers. Provide SDK quickstart repo with examples for: auth (OIDC + service token fallback), fetch -> rerank piping, structured output for the reranker response. (ETA: 3 business days.)
2) Eval run (owner: BrightCart + Marissa): BrightCart provides anonymized eval set; Redwood runs batch embedding + recall/DCG comparison between 768 baseline and candidate 1024 embeddings. We’ll produce a report with per-query latency percentiles and cost delta. (ETA: 5–7 business days after eval set delivery.)
3) Indexing + canary (owner: Redwood infra + BrightCart): bulk reindex to 1024 in a side index, run shadow traffic, then enable 5% canary. Monitor: P99 latency, DCG lift, token & compute cost.
4) Production migration (owner: BrightCart + Redwood): schedule cutoff, warm caches, throttle reindex to avoid burst overage. Provide rollback steps and retention window.

SDK/auth notes (Karthik to follow with sample flows):
- Use OIDC for console/interactive flows; issue short-lived service tokens for backend calls.
- Recommend token rotation schedule and an allowlist for sandbox IPs.
- Routing policy: canary rule by header (x-redwood-canary) or by traffic percentage via route config.

Attachments: I’m attaching a one-page quick checklist and the SOW draft Sergio sent with light edits. Also included our standard sandbox onboarding doc as sandbox-invite.txt.

If Tue/Wed mornings PT work, I’ll block 30 minutes Tue 09:30 PT for a technical kickoff with Karthik and one of our infra engineers.

—Marissa
